t: Pizarro founded Lima in 1535 in a valley that the Ichma, the Wari and then the Inca had held, and in 1543 it became the capital of the Viceroyalty of Peru.
It grew rich in the 17th century on the silver trade through Callao, then lost ground to earthquakes, new viceroyalties and the Bourbon Reforms, and in 1821 it became the capital of independent Peru.
Migration from the Andes from the 1940s made it one of the largest cities of South America, and it is now the capital of Peru, holding about a third of the country's people in its metropolitan area.
dyk: The name Lima probably comes from Limaq, the name of a famous oracle in the Rímac valley that the Spanish destroyed and replaced with a church.
ev: Francisco Pizarro founds the City of Kings in the Rímac valley
Troops sent by Manco Inca besiege the city and are defeated by the Spanish and their indigenous allies
Lima becomes the capital of the Viceroyalty of Peru and the seat of a Real Audiencia
Earthquakes on 20 October and 2 December destroy most of the city
An earthquake severely damages Lima and destroys Callao
The viceroy leaves, and the city council signs a Declaration of Independence at the request of San Martín
The War of the Pacific begins, and Chilean troops later occupy and loot the city
An earthquake strikes, and rapid growth from migration from the Andes begins

f.founded: Francisco Pizarro founded the city in 1535 as the City of Kings, on land that had belonged to the local lord Taulichusco, in a valley long held by the Ichma polity.
f.where: In the valleys of the Chillón, Rímac and Lurín rivers on the desert coast of central Peru, overlooking the Pacific Ocean, with the port of Callao beside it.
f.known: The Spanish City of Kings; capital of the Viceroyalty of Peru; the silver trade through Callao; the earthquake of 1687; the oldest continuously operating university of the New World; the Lord of Miracles procession; the Historic Centre
f.today: Lima is the capital and largest city of Peru, with about 10 million inhabitants, and its historic centre is a World Heritage Site.
